decisions.question: Routed item: G14's 'a handle another builder made' needs a handle-to-builder link. Which link?

options.label: A private final field set by TopicStream's private constructor
options.consequence: TopicStream._(this._builder); every stage constructor passes the builder as super.builder; ownership is identical(handle._builder, this); a handle method also finds the builder to record into. Changes eighteen private constructors in Task 1.

options.label: An Expando<TopologyBuilder> keyed by handle
options.consequence: No constructor changes, but a weak side table the builder fills and every handle method looks up; ownership and recording go through a map lookup.

options.label: An identity set of handles in each builder
options.consequence: Answers ownership, but a handle method still needs its own builder to record into, so it does not remove the link.

decisions.chosen: A private final field set by TopicStream's private constructor
decisions.why: The routed item names the first two; the field is plain immutable data on an immutable stage, needs no lookup, and is what a handle method needs anyway. Seeded defect D6 (ownership by a closed builder instead of identity) shows the identity test is what tells an open foreign builder apart.

decisions.question: Routed item: CombineStage.apply for combineAll needs T, which CombineStage<R> does not carry. How does apply call the combiner?

options.label: A typed closure for every combine and withLatestFrom call
options.consequence: Each builder or handle call captures R Function(List<Object?>) (or R Function(T, List<Object?>)) built from its own type arguments; apply casts each value to its input's type, and combineAll's closure hands the combiner List<T>.unmodifiable(values.cast<T>()). Two private fields, no dynamic call.

options.label: Function.apply for combine2 to combine4, a closure for combineAll only
options.consequence: Fewer closures, but a dynamic invocation with no casts at the declared types, and two mechanisms for one method.

options.label: A dynamic call of combiner
options.consequence: Fails for combineAll: a List<Object?> is not a List<int> (F C1).

decisions.chosen: A typed closure for every combine and withLatestFrom call
decisions.why: F C1 to C5 show the List<Object?> failure and that a copy made in a captured closure is typed and unmodifiable; one mechanism for all arities keeps apply a two-line method. D2 (a modifiable cast view) passes the suite and fails the package test.

decisions.question: What does apply do with a value list whose length is not the number of inputs? The contract leaves it open.

options.label: Throw ArgumentError
options.consequence: An interpreter's off-by-one shows at once; combineAll's combiner never sees extra values.

options.label: No check
options.consequence: Too few values fail with a RangeError from inside the closure; too many are silently ignored by combine2 to combine4 and passed through by combineAll.

decisions.why: A precondition check costs one comparison and turns a silent misread into an error. D10 showed that only a too-many case tells the check from its absence (RangeError is an ArgumentError), so the test uses one. A contract statement would change nothing here; reported as a gap for a compatible touch.

decisions.question: In what order does a call check, and when does it record?

options.label: Open builder first, then arguments, record last
options.consequence: A closed builder gives StateError whatever the arguments (the contract says every method throws StateError once declare returned); a rejected call leaves no stage, consumes no handle, claims no topic.

options.label: Argument checks first
options.consequence: A closed builder given a negative duration throws ArgumentError, contradicting 'every builder and handle method throws StateError'.

options.label: Record, then check
options.consequence: A rejected call leaves a stage nothing consumes; a declaration that catches the error then fails planOf with a misleading StateError.

decisions.chosen: Open builder first, then arguments, record last
decisions.why: The phase's Verification line asks each misuse to throw at the call that commits it, not later; D3, D8 and D9 seed the two wrong orders, the suite passes all three, and the package tests fail them.

decisions.question: How does planOf decide that a stage reaches no sink (G15)?

options.label: A consumed set: every stage must be an input of a later stage or of a sink
options.consequence: One identity set filled as stages and sinks are recorded; equivalent to reachability because a stage's inputs precede it, so a chain of consumers moves forward and ends at a stage a sink consumes.

options.label: A walk back from the sinks
options.consequence: Needs each stage's inputs as a list, an extra private getter on all eighteen classes or a visitor.

options.label: A forward graph
options.consequence: More code for the same answer.

decisions.chosen: A consumed set: every stage must be an input of a later stage or of a sink
decisions.why: The equivalence holds by construction (inputs precede their stage, G11) and the record already has every input at hand; the suite's two G15 shapes and the package tests (a read alone, a map off a written read, a pairwise chain) pass.

decisions.question: When does planOf check the id, and how does it close the builder?

options.label: Id before declare; close in a finally
options.consequence: An empty id runs nothing; a handle kept from a declaration that threw records nothing more.

options.label: Id after declare; close on normal return
options.consequence: declare runs for an invalid topology, and a leaked handle of a failed declaration stays usable.

decisions.chosen: Id before declare; close in a finally
decisions.why: G15 says a builder or handle used after declare returned throws StateError; a throw is a return from declare. D5 seeds the normal-return close: the suite passes, the package test fails.

decisions.question: How do visitStage and visitSink bind the stage's type arguments (G16)?

options.label: A private _accept each class implements
options.consequence: visitor.map<T, R>(this) inside MapStage<T, R>: the stage's own type arguments, checked by the compiler for all eighteen classes because _accept is abstract in the sealed base.

options.label: An exhaustive switch in visitStage
options.consequence: Each case sees the stage at Object? type arguments, so the visitor is called at Object? and reading a function member through such a pattern throws TypeError (F V4).

decisions.why: F V1 to V4 show the binding through _accept and the TypeError through a pattern; D1 (a visitor called at Object?) passes the whole recording suite and fails only the package test, so the plan writes the type arguments out.

decisions.question: How does the one-sink-per-StateTopic check compare topics?

options.label: A Set<StateTopic<Object?>> under topic equality
options.consequence: Two state topics with one name and value type built apart are one topic (topic-model@v1 G7); another value type is another topic.

options.label: An identity set
options.consequence: Two declarations of one topic, from two registries or a non-const construction, each get a sink.

decisions.why: The phase's Dependencies line says the check uses nidana.model.8's topic equality; D4 seeds identity: the suite passes (it writes one const topic twice), the package test fails.

decisions.question: What does a stage keep of an input list the declaration passed (combine inputs, merge inputs, withLatestFrom latest)?

options.label: An unmodifiable copy
options.consequence: Later changes to the caller's list do not reach the stage; the handles inside are identical.

options.label: An unmodifiable view of the caller's list
options.consequence: No copy, but a declaration that reuses its list changes the recorded stage.

decisions.why: G11 asks the stage to hold the handles it was given and the Interface calls the lists unmodifiable; topic-model@v1 G4 set the same rule for its values. D7 seeds keeping the caller's list: the suite passes, the package tests fail.

options.consequence: Each task's code makes its own failing tests pass and turns its own suite cases green (7, 2, 7, 3); intermediate library states analyze clean.

options.label: Seven tasks with the misuse checks and G10 on their own
options.consequence: The misuse checks live in the methods that commit them, so a separate task would reopen every method; G10 has no code of its own.

decisions.question: How do the package's tests assert 'creates no timer and schedules no microtask' without a new dependency?

options.label: runZoned with a ZoneSpecification counting createTimer, createPeriodicTimer and scheduleMicrotask, with a positive control
options.consequence: dart:async only; the test first shows the counter counts a timer and a microtask (2), then that recording every combinator counts 0.

options.label: fake_async
options.consequence: Not in ADR-002's table for nidana_dart_contracts (meta and test only).
